# our_file: impl/linalg/detail/pca.mojo::whiten_scale_kernel + whiten_components + whiten_scalar
upstream_file: cuml cpp/src/pca/pca.cuh::pcaTransform whiten arm (:292-302) and pcaInverseTransform whiten arm (:232-243); the same two calls at the 26.08 pin are raft cpp/include/raft/linalg/detail/pca.cuh:233-243 and :301-311
notes: theirs is TWO device passes over a copy of the components, raft::linalg::scalarMultiply then raft::matrix::matrixVectorBinaryDivSkipZero (matrix/detail/math.cuh:236-272) or ...MultSkipZero (:209-225); ours is ONE kernel doing both, which is a launch-count change and not an arithmetic one because the elided intermediate is a float32 store followed by a float32 load and `ftz` makes that exact on a denormal-honoring column too. FIVE DEVIATIONS, all in the file's block comment: 580 the row count is the FIT's and not the transform call's (cuML's dense path is inconsistent with its own sparse path and with scikit-learn, so it is their bug); 581 one skip threshold in both directions, where theirs uses `abs(s) < 1e-10` forward and `s == 0` inverse and is therefore not round-trip exact; 582 cuML's skip rather than scikit-learn's clamp to eps (_base.py:164-168); 583 the scalar is host float64 rounded once, which is what math_t(sqrt(int)) does in C++; 584 identical_mul / identical_div / ftz at the seam, so the rescale runs in all three tiers
